metadata.title: Palantir Hires Former UK Labour Veteran With NHS Deal in Limbo

content.text:
(Bloomberg) -- Palantir Technologies Inc. has hired Tom Watson, a former Labour deputy leader, as a new executive in the UK, where it faces a barrage of criticism threatening a major contract.

The veteran politician, who left the House of Commons in 2019, will serve as Palantir's UK senior vice president, the software developer and major military vendor said on Friday. In that role, the company said he will lead efforts to make sure public contracts "support British jobs" across the entire country, a key priority of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Watson has been an adviser to Palantir since 2024.
The UK, Palantir's second-largest market after the US, has been both lucrative and politically rocky for the company. Palantir won a marquee £330 million ($441 million) contract for the National Health Service in 2023, then added a prominent deal with Britain's defense ministry.
Yet, the expansion has come with controversy. Critics have targeted Palantir's data-mining business model, its work with Israel and its proximity to the administration of US President Donald Trump. Scrutiny has grown in the UK as politicians are increasingly worried about a reliance on American technology.
In June, British parliamentarians called for the government to cancel Palantir's NHS contract, citing concerns about tech sovereignty and comments from company co-founder Peter Thiel. The politicians proposed using a break clause to end the contract and finding a British alternative by the end of the year.
Burnham, who took over the Labour party in July, hasn't indicated if he will break the contract.
In his 18-year career in the Commons, Watson served in Gordon Brown's government as a digital minister under Burnham at the Department for Culture, Media and Sport in 2008 and 2009. Watson then returned to the back benches after Labour's electoral defeat in 2010. As a member of the House of Commons Culture, Media and Sport Committee, he was instrumental in the probe of the News International phone hacking scandal, grilling tycoon Rupert Murdoch during hearings.
Watson later served in the shadow cabinet under Jeremy Corbyn, an embattled leader with whom Watson frequently sparred.
